items.title: Petit Ours Brun
items.why: Two-minute stories about a little bear's day: one simple sentence at a time, with the pictures showing everything.

items.title: Coffee Break French
items.whereToFind: Any podcast app (free; extras with a subscription)
items.why: A teacher and a learner build up French from the very first words, explaining everything in English. Good for a commute.

items.title: Peppa Pig (French)
items.why: Short, very clear episodes about everyday life. Easy input like this builds speed and confidence.

items.title: Trotro
items.why: Three-minute episodes about a little donkey's day, in slow, simple sentences. Made for small children, so every word is everyday French.

items.title: Alice Ayel
items.why: Stories told slowly with drawings, made to be understood without translating. A gentle way into listening to real French.

items.title: Super Easy French
items.whereToFind: YouTube: Easy French channel, "Super Easy French" playlist
items.why: Simple street conversations on one topic at a time, spoken slowly, with French and English subtitles.

items.title: 1 jour, 1 question
items.why: Ninety-second cartoons that answer a child's question about the world. Clear narration and pictures that explain every idea.

items.title: Little Talk in Slow French
items.why: Short episodes about daily life and culture, spoken slowly and clearly. Good for a walk or a commute.

items.title: Duolingo French Podcast
items.why: True stories told in clear French, with short English narration that keeps you on track.

items.title: Le Petit Nicolas
items.whereToFind: YouTube: search "Le Petit Nicolas dessin animé"
items.why: A cartoon about a schoolboy and his friends, from the classic books. Everyday family and school French, with stories that are easy to follow.

items.title: Ratatouille
items.why: You may know the story already, which makes the French easier to follow. Set in Paris, with lots of food and kitchen vocabulary.

items.title: InnerFrench
items.whereToFind: Any podcast app or YouTube; free transcripts on the website
items.why: Hugo talks about society, psychology and culture in clear, natural French, a little slower than normal. Made to take you from learner material to real content.

items.title: Easy French
items.why: Street interviews with ordinary people in Paris. Real, unscripted French with subtitles in French and English.

items.title: French Mornings with Elisa
items.why: Short videos entirely in French about how people really speak: expressions, pronunciation and everyday situations.

items.title: Français Authentique
items.why: Johan talks about personal growth, French culture and learning, in clear French at a steady pace. Hundreds of episodes.

items.title: Journal en français facile
items.whereToFind: Any podcast app, or the RFI website with transcripts
items.why: Ten minutes of world news from RFI every day, in simpler French than a normal bulletin. The transcript helps you check what you missed.

items.title: C'est pas sorcier
items.why: A much-loved science show: two presenters explain how things work with models and experiments. Clear speech, and the pictures carry you.

items.title: Les Choristes
items.whereToFind: Streaming and rental services (varies by country)
items.why: A new teacher starts a choir in a strict boarding school. Clear dialogue, a simple story, and songs you'll remember.

items.title: Intouchables
items.whereToFind: Netflix in many countries, or rental
items.why: The friendship between a wealthy man and his carer. Funny and warm, with a mix of formal and everyday spoken French.

items.title: HugoDécrypte
items.why: The day's news explained in ten minutes for a young French audience. Fast, natural speech on topics you may already know.

items.title: Lupin
items.why: A gentleman thief in modern Paris. Gripping enough to keep you watching, with clear, contemporary French.

items.title: Dix pour cent (Call My Agent!)
items.why: A comedy set in a Paris talent agency. Fast office and everyday French, with lots of humour.

items.title: Plan Cœur (The Hook Up Plan)
items.why: A romantic comedy about friends in Paris. How young adults really talk: informal, quick and full of slang.

items.title: Au service de la France (A Very Secret Service)
items.why: A dry comedy about French spies in the 1960s. Precise, formal French, so it's easier to follow than most series.

items.title: Transfert
items.why: One person tells one true story from their life in each episode. Natural speech, one voice at a time, and stories that hold you.

items.title: Les Pieds sur terre
items.why: Half-hour documentaries made only of ordinary people's voices, from all over France. Many accents and ways of speaking.

items.title: Le Bureau des légendes (The Bureau)
items.whereToFind: Canal+; other services vary by country
items.why: A spy drama inside French intelligence. Dense, fast dialogue: a real test once Netflix comedies feel comfortable.
